title: Search a 2D Matrix
summary: Given an m x n matrix where each row is sorted in non-decreasing order and the first element of each row is greater than the last element of the previous row, determine if a given target integer is present in the matrix.
statement: Given an m x n matrix where each row is sorted in non-decreasing order and the first element of each row is greater than the last element of the previous row, determine if a given target integer is present in the matrix. The solution must be implemented with a time complexity of O(log(m * n)).
constraints: A rectangular grid has 1–100 rows and columns. Values and target are in [-10,000,10,000].
Rows are nondecreasing; each row starts with a value strictly greater than the previous row's final value.
hints: The row-boundary rule makes the entire row-major sequence sorted.
Binary-search a virtual array without allocating a flattened copy.
Translate midpoint to row=mid//column_count and column=mid%column_count, then update the usual search bounds.
Use the number of columns for index conversion, including rectangular and single-column grids.
editorial: Treat the grid as one sorted sequence of length m×n. Its index i refers to matrix[i//n][i%n]. Binary-search this virtual sequence, retaining the equality case and examining the final remaining candidate. No flattening is needed, so the auxiliary space is constant. A linear scan serves as an independent correctness oracle, not as the reference complexity target.

tests.explanation: The target 3 occurs at row zero, column one.
13 lies between 11 and 16 but is not present, so return false.
